account.title: Credits & storage
agent.askConsent: This sends what you type — and the rest of this conversation, for as long as it lasts — to Anthropic, who run the model. To answer, it may look up facts from this journal: your trips, what is unfinished, a day's own words, what a trip cost, your storage and your credits. Nothing else goes: not your photographs, not your location history, not your contacts, not anybody's address. It cannot change anything by itself. What it can do is propose — a trip, a day, its words, a cost, putting a day on the site or taking it off — and each of those is fields on your screen with a button you press; nothing is written until you do. It cannot delete anything at all, and it cannot send a postcard. Asking is free, and the one proposal that costs a credit says so before you press. Your words are not used to train anybody's model. This is remembered for this journal until you withdraw it.
agent.askConsentShort: Sends what you type, and what it looks up in this journal, to a model. It can read and answer, never change. Free.

agent.askRefusePublishAll: Publishing everything at once is not something this box does, and nothing has changed. A day goes on the site one at a time, after somebody has read it back — so say which day you mean, by its date or by what it is called, and the next answer shows you that day as your readers will see it, with the button underneath. If you are not sure how many are waiting, ask which days are still drafts and we will go through them one at a time.
agent.askRefuseRemove: Deleting is not something this conversation can do, and nothing has changed. A photograph, a day, a trip or a whole journal that you want gone is asked for elsewhere: deleting a journal or a trip finishes in your email, where the server sends a single-use link to a page with a button, and only that button deletes. If you meant taking a day off the site rather than destroying it, say that instead — a day can be taken down here, and nothing is lost by it.

agent.intro: This is where you sign in to start a day, or hand your journal to an agent of your own.
agent.introWhy: Everything an agent writes waits as a draft until you publish it, so you read a day before anybody else can. Publishing is your decision and nobody else's, and you can take a day down again at any time.

agent.noAccessYet: I cannot tell you that somebody can read this. A trip that is not public is open to the people who were on it and to the guests you have approved — naming somebody does not let them in. Say who should read it and I will put a link in front of you to send them.

agent.photoConsent: This sends the photographs on this day — resized copies, not the originals — to Anthropic, who run the model, so it can suggest a caption for each one. Nothing else goes: not your location history, not your contacts, not anybody's address, and not a trip you did not open. It will not name a place it recognises, guess who anyone is, or guess a mood — only describe what is visibly in the frame, and it may say nothing at all. What comes back is shown to you to read and keep or discard; nothing is saved until you save it. This costs one credit per ten photographs, rounding up. Your photographs are not used to train anybody's model. This is remembered for this journal until you withdraw it, separately from consent to send your words.

If you may want it later, hide it instead — that takes it off the site and keeps the file. A photobook or postcard already ordered is untouched; it is a record of what was sent, not a live link.

agent.speechConsent: This sends the recording you are about to make — your voice, and nothing else — to {provider}, who turn it into text. Not your photographs, not your location history, not your contacts, not anybody's address. The recording is not kept: it is transcribed and dropped, and no copy of it is written down anywhere on this server. The words come back into the box for you to read and change, and nothing is saved until you save it. It costs one credit per {minutes} started minutes. Your voice is not used to train anybody's model. This is remembered for this journal until you withdraw it, separately from consent to send your words or your photographs.
agent.speechConsentDryRun: This sends the recording you are about to make to the built-in dry-run backend — nothing leaves this server, no third party ever hears it, and the text you get back is a canned placeholder rather than a real transcript. It costs one credit per {minutes} started minutes, same as the real thing, so testing the flow costs the same as using it. This is remembered for this journal until you withdraw it, separately from consent to send your words or your photographs.

agent.statementConsent: This sends the heading row of this file and its first five rows — and nothing else — to Anthropic, who run the model, so it can say which column is the date, which the amount, which the currency and which the description. The rest of the file stays on this server: whatever its length, it is read here, by this software, using what comes back. Nothing else goes either — not your other files, not your location history, not your contacts, not anybody's address. What comes back is shown to you to correct before a single cost is written. It costs {credits} credit, once, however long the statement is. Nothing you send is used to train anybody's model. This is remembered for this journal until you withdraw it, separately from consent to send your words, your photographs or your voice.

me.tokenBody: A key from here — or a code you read out — becomes a key that works for seven days, on this journal and nothing else. It can write days, and it can put one on the site when you ask it to; everything it writes waits as a draft until you do. It is the whole of your editing, which is why it goes to somebody you trust and never into a group chat.
me.tokenWarning: None of it is the same as being signed in here. Reading your journal in this browser cannot change it — a key can, and anyone holding one can use it. A key lasts seven days, and an agent still working can renew itself before then, so revoking is how one ends for certain.

welcome.public: It is public: it is listed on this server’s own index and search engines may index it. Each journey still decides for itself whether anyone can read it, and a new one here starts out public too, unless you ask for something narrower.
